text: So Moses told the Israelites everything just as the LORD had commanded him.
Moses said to the heads of the tribes of Israel: This is what the LORD has commanded.
When a man makes a vow to the LORD or swears an oath binding himself by a pledge, he must not break his word. He must do everything he has said.
When a young woman still living in her father's house makes a vow to the LORD or binds herself by a pledge,
and her father hears about her vow and the pledge by which she has bound herself, and he says nothing to her, then all her vows stand, and every pledge by which she has bound herself stands.

versions.text: and her father hears about her vow or the pledge by which she has bound herself, and he says nothing to her, then all her vows stand, and every pledge by which she has bound herself stands.
versions.explanation: The Hebrew joins vow and pledge with "and" (waw), not "or"; the father hears both together. The "or" needlessly separates them.

text: But if her father forbids her on the day he hears of it, then none of her vows or the pledges by which she has bound herself will stand. The LORD will forgive her, because her father has forbidden her.

versions.text: But if her father forbids her on the day he hears of it, then none of her vows or the pledges by which she has bound herself will stand. The LORD will release her, because her father has forbidden her.
versions.explanation: The Hebrew verb סלח means "forgive" (it is the standard verb for divine pardon). "Release her" flattens the theological point that God pardons her for the unfulfilled vow. A footnote could note the sense "release her from the obligation."

text: If she marries while under a vow, or under some rash promise from her lips by which she has bound herself,
and her husband hears of it and says nothing to her on the day he hears, then her vows stand, and the pledges by which she has bound herself stand.
But if her husband forbids her on the day he hears of it, he nullifies the vow that binds her and the rash promise of her lips by which she bound herself, and the LORD will forgive her.

versions.text: But if her husband forbids her on the day he hears of it, he nullifies the vow that binds her and the rash promise of her lips by which she bound herself, and the LORD will release her.
versions.explanation: Same as verse 6: סלח means "forgive." Consistency of this key phrase across verses 6, 9, and 13 matters for oral reading and for accuracy.

text: Any vow of a widow or a divorced woman, everything by which she has bound herself, is binding on her.

versions.text: Any vow of a widow or a divorced woman, everything by which she has bound herself, stands against her.
versions.explanation: "Stands against her" sounds accusatory in English; the idiom יקום עליה means the obligation remains in force upon her, i.e. "is binding on her." This also reads more smoothly aloud.

text: If a woman living with her husband makes a vow or binds herself by a pledge under oath,
and her husband hears of it and says nothing to her and does not forbid her, then all her vows stand, and every pledge by which she has bound herself stands.

But if her husband nullifies them on the day he hears of them, then nothing that came from her lips, whether vows or pledges binding herself, will stand. Her husband has nullified them, and the LORD will forgive her.

versions.text: But if her husband nullifies them on the day he hears of them, then nothing that came from her lips, whether vows or pledges binding herself, will stand. Her husband has nullified them, and the LORD will release her.
versions.explanation: Same as verses 6 and 9: the Hebrew states that the LORD forgives her, not merely that he releases her.

text: Her husband may confirm or nullify any vow she makes or any sworn pledge to deny herself.

But if her husband says nothing to her about it from one day to the next, then he confirms all her vows or all the pledges binding her. He confirms them by saying nothing to her on the day he hears of them.
If, however, he nullifies them some time after he hears of them, then he bears her guilt.
These are the statutes the LORD commanded Moses concerning a man and his wife, and a father and his young daughter still living in his house.
